summary: The last 4 weeks show an inconsistent training block with very low volume overall — only 8 sessions logged, dominated by indoor cardio (likely yoga/pilates) and two open-water swims, with a single run and limited cycling. Sleep is severely compromised, with multiple nights under 4 hours and body battery frequently depleted, indicating accumulated fatigue that must be addressed before the 5K Open Water race on October 25. The nearest priority race (5K OW Swim, 8 days away) is reasonably supported by two recent open-water swims including a 5.2km effort on Oct 3, but run and bike volume is far below what the marathon and Ironman targets will eventually demand.
suggestions: Sleep is your biggest performance limiter right now — multiple nights of 3 hours or less and near-zero body battery readings suggest you are chronically under-recovered; prioritise 7–8 hours per night this week as non-negotiable race prep for October 25.

Your Oct 3 open-water 5.2km at 136bpm avg is a solid confidence builder for the 5K race — do one short, race-pace open-water or pool session (1,500–2,000m) mid-week to stay sharp without accumulating fatigue before Oct 25.

Run mileage is critically low for a sub-4h marathon in 113 days — after the 5K swim race, build a consistent run frequency of 3 sessions per week immediately, keeping easy runs at 6:30–7:00/km to establish the aerobic base before introducing pace work.

The Oct 17 long ride (80km, 240 min) falls the day before the AI-adjusted long run and only 8 days before a race — keep the ride but cap it at 60–70km and strictly hold Z2 watts (128–177W) with no tempo blocks this week to protect freshness for Oct 25.

Power data on the Sep 25 run shows 333W with avg HR 169 and pace only 6:15/km — this disproportionately high effort-to-pace ratio suggests either significant fatigue or elevated stress on that day; monitor run HR trends closely and avoid repeating high-HR efforts at slow paces, as this pattern can signal overreach.

proposed_changes.reason: Race is 8 days away and sleep/body battery data show chronic under-recovery; reducing ride volume protects freshness for the Oct 25 5K OW Swim without sacrificing aerobic stimulus.

proposed_changes.reason: Given the critically low run training volume over the past 4 weeks, jumping to 18.8km the week after a race creates a significant injury risk; 15km is a safer progression toward the marathon base needed in 113 days.
